extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of humor; writers, literary critics, and performers studying humor theory
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying theoretical criteria that distinguish practical (situation-based) humor from poetic (language/quality-based) humor, and identifying features that make jokes, puns, repartee, naive blunders, and poetic incongruities effective. Useful for literary analysis, writing, or performance design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distance from real anguish
rubrics_metrics.description: We are not able to perceive any loss entailing real anguish as humorous, unless the persons involved are far away, or long dead, or imaginary, and we merely hear the tale of their troubles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emotional distance or detachment is a precondition for finding serious misfortune funny; actual immediate suffering resists playful reception. Use distance (temporal, spatial, or fictionalization) when turning painful situations into humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical humor as playful disappointment
rubrics_metrics.description: The interior result in its negative aspect is essentially the same: it is a disappointment which for some reason we are able to take playfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical jokes often work by setting up an expectation and converting it into a 'nothing' or failure that is nevertheless playfully received (example: family dressed for church but horse refuses to move). The comic effect comes from the conversion of expectation into an absurd absence of the anticipated event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared predicament / sympathetic reverberation
rubrics_metrics.description: The most hilarious of practical laughter arises when all of those present are involved in the same predicament, and the humor is increased through sympathetic reverberation without the possibility of derision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor is amplified when everyone shares the predicament (no single target of derision). Design situations where the audience recognizes themselves collectively in the failing or absurdity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absurdity as 'reduction to absurdity' (Irish bull / bulla)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is an absurd situation ... a 'reduction to absurdity' of the whole attitude of our wills. 'Irish bull' defined as any remark which appears rotund and meaningful enough, until our apprehension actually arrives upon it, when there is simply nothing there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absurdity often stems from plausibility that collapses into nothing on inspection. A good 'bull' has surface plausibility that yields a comic absence of substance; authors can craft this by leading the audience to expect meaning and then revealing vacuum or contradiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit = combining 'nothing' with a positive discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Such happy combinations, when deliberately perpetrated in conversation, we describe as wit. A witty joker may be likened to a man who ... contrives to trip us up in such a way that we shall find [a gold piece]. To stumble and find something is to enjoy a joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wit differs from mere emptiness by delivering an extra 'something' (a discovery, a turned meaning). In practice, construct jokes that lead the audience to a stumbling point but then reward them with a satisfying unexpected payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of repartee
rubrics_metrics.description: One contestant propounds a thesis giving glory to himself or ignominy to his opponent; the opponent manipulates the implications so the propounder's glory disappears and his own appears; the propounder then tries to restore his glory; and so on until one cries enough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repartee is a back-and-forth game of implication-reversal. Good repartee manipulates the conversational premises to reverse status, and success depends on rapid, logical turns that expose and invert the other's claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit is not merely 'eluding of a censorship'
rubrics_metrics.description: Freud would have us believe that the pith of this wit lies in the 'eluding of a censorship' — saying a thing indirectly which good manners would otherwise prohibit. But humor lay in the fact that the minister went to hell on the wings of his own logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid equating indirectness or taboo-evading speech with the essence of wit; stronger humor arises when an opponent's own logic is used to undermine them, rather than merely sneaking past social prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naive blunder produces affectionate pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: A naive blunder can give a shock which might be displeasure to those who enjoy its humor, and give a rich and positive pleasure besides. It presents the blunderer (e.g., a schoolboy trying earnestly) and arouses tender sympathy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naive mistakes can be 'beautiful' because they offer positive satisfactions (loving an innocent mind, glorying over it, realizing wished-for things). When using naive blunders for humor, foreground the actor's innocence or earnestness to elicit affectionate laughter rather than contempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Puns: negative action vs affirmative recompense
rubrics_metrics.description: The play upon words, the pun, is the form of practical wit most remote from poetic humor. The negative action of a pun is merely the nonsensical use of a word; we need not pay them much respect unless they offer some good strong joy in the recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Puns that merely produce nonsense feel graceless and alien; to be genuinely humorous a pun should provide an affirmative reward (a meaningful double-take, clever recovery, or emotional payoff). Otherwise, treat puns sparingly or supplement them with additional value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic humor methods: inappropriate choice (salient detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry chooses some salient detail or flavor in things upon which we may focus our attention. In poetic humor there is an art of inappropriate choice — naming an object by a salient but playfully incongruous detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To create poetic humor via choice, select a salient attribute that is oddly inappropriate or disproportionate for naming or describing the object (example: Dante's 'One who left off singing hallelujahs' or O. Henry's 'One at whose bidding many lobsters had perished'). The incongruity between attribute and whole produces comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic humor methods: incongruous comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetic language makes vivid by comparing things which are similar in some salient detail. Poetic humor exploits playfully incongruous comparisons (example: Aristophanes' 'a voice like a pig on fire').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft similes/metaphors that juxtapose emotionally incompatible images; the explosive mismatch between images yields poetic laughter. Ensure both ends are lightly taken (not solemn) to keep the effect playful rather than scornful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic humor foregrounds qualities and endures without a point
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetic jokes differ from practical ones in their more enduring ability to provoke laughter without a point. A mere incongruity presenting an actual thing (not just a vacancy) will tickle us more strongly than a mere bull.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetic humor often lingers and can be appreciated for its image or tone alone. When aiming for poetic humor, emphasize vivid, concrete, and oddly combined qualities rather than relying solely on setup-punch structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance poetic humor: mimetic gesture and pathos (Chaplin model)
rubrics_metrics.description: A gift for acting as though a present thing were something else, and acting so vividly that the absent thing flashes actually before us, is almost the essential principle in Chaplin’s art. He is a humorous poet who is also a great actor — a master of mimetic gesture and expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In performance, achieve poetic humor by embodying incongruities with gesture and expression that make the absent or imagined image palpably present; combine pathos and comic inappropriateness to produce pity-comedy and sustained audience empathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humorous liberty: relief of tension in solemn contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: We laugh more generously at a humorous thing which 'really happened' than at the same thing if it is offered as a 'funny story.' The unchaining of the little child within us and the relief of tension in solemn contexts constitute 'humorous liberty.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit the contrast between solemn expectation and inadvertent levity (church, ceremonies, funerals) to generate a strong relief-laughter. Real-life authenticity of the incident increases the effect; editors/performers should present such moments as 'it really happened' when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic truth from alternate viewpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetic truth from some other point of view: the external world is so patient of our whims that it is willing to be many different things according as we choose to perceive it (example: Turner painting as 'The Slave-Ship' or 'A tortoise-shell cat having a fit in a platter of tomatoes').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leveraging alternate but defensible perceptions of the same object yields comic insight and delight. Encourage audience imaginative sympathy by proposing a fresh, vivid reframing that reveals a new, amusing 'truth' about a familiar scene.
